proposed_seasons.question: 공장·제품·기술을 누가 소유하고, 누가 제조와 출하 위험을 부담하는가?
proposed_seasons.engine: A material handoff crosses company boundaries; reveal the liability that did not move.
proposed_seasons.style: Stainless-steel architecture, observed actions, ownership boundaries, dated corporate records; neutral documentary illumination.
proposed_seasons.pitfall: Keep R8 in-progress film, do not visually imply private factory access or universal foundry contract terms.

proposed_seasons.question: 물리적·아키텍처적 한계가 다음 설계를 언제 유리하게 만드는가?
proposed_seasons.engine: Start at a performance puzzle, reveal its physical trace, then the alternative architecture and price.
proposed_seasons.style: Signal timelines, energy envelopes, transistor cutaways, archival experiment cards; not generic glowing chip loops.
proposed_seasons.motifs: signal→latency→heat→choice; same GPU returns between E01/E06/E08
proposed_seasons.pitfall: E01 and E06 are separated by canon: link by dated experiment callback, not claim identical GPU architecture or hardware.

proposed_seasons.question: 비트를 반복해서 만들고 팔 때 실제 비용과 대가는 무엇인가?
proposed_seasons.engine: Follow the physical bit into a distinct cost ledger: labor, area, yield, qualification, price or learning.
proposed_seasons.style: Tactile hardware and archival tools, annotated cell geometry, sparse cost comparisons with real units.
proposed_seasons.motifs: one bit→one cell→one wafer→one factory decision
proposed_seasons.pitfall: Do not use one universal cost-per-bit series or imply national outcomes have a single cause.

proposed_seasons.question: 국가의 조달·협력·규제가 실제 칩, 재료, 공정과 거래를 어떻게 바꾸는가?
proposed_seasons.engine: Start from an archived decision/document, traverse the affected material or device, compare interests and dated outcomes.
proposed_seasons.style: Dated source plates, clear regional maps, physical qualification gates, restrained institutional document animation.
proposed_seasons.pitfall: No fake intelligence access, fabricated regulators, prediction theater or undated legal status.

episodes.candidate_title: The Factory That Doesn't Promise a Chip
episodes.narrative_tension: Idle tool versus a wafer still waiting: who can actually deliver a working chip?
episodes.picture_concept: One carrier enters a qualified-route gate; the manufacturer/designer obligations diverge over the same physical wafer.
episodes.evidence_gate: Respect PR #4 R8 as an IN_REVIEW existing production; use 1997 TSMC and 1998 NVIDIA filings in dated context; no new shot approval.

episodes.candidate_title: What Eight Resignations Changed
episodes.narrative_tension: Leaving an employer is a decision; turning expertise into a repeatable industry is the harder act.
episodes.picture_concept: Eight workstations go dark; a dated corporate/organizational map emerges from independently sourced founder records.
episodes.evidence_gate: No dramatized removal of proprietary notebooks; distinguish oral histories from signed records.

episodes.candidate_title: Why AMD Let Go of Its Fabs
episodes.narrative_tension: What capital burden and manufacturing dependency remain when a chip business changes its ownership boundary?
episodes.picture_concept: A single fab shown as two contractual ledgers: asset ownership leaves, wafer commitments remain.
episodes.evidence_gate: AMD/GlobalFoundries transaction terms and wafer supply terms must be dated; no universal fabless claim.

episodes.candidate_title: How Taiwan Learned to Repeat a Process
episodes.narrative_tension: Technology transfer delivers knowledge, not instant production capability.
episodes.picture_concept: Training map leads into successive illustrative qualification lots, with unknown yield values left blank.
episodes.evidence_gate: Confirm RCA/ITRI records and named engineers; no invented factory footage or numerical yield curve.

episodes.candidate_title: Independence Has a Process Cost
episodes.narrative_tension: What would it cost to own the recipe instead of following someone else's?
episodes.picture_concept: Two copper-integration routes enter a reliability-testing fork; a documented/no-evidence ledger stays visible.
episodes.evidence_gate: Unverified 'turned down IBM' story stays a research question; no filmed rejection without direct evidence.

episodes.candidate_title: The Factory Behind a Phone Chip
episodes.narrative_tension: Why does a fabless vendor still need a manufacturing network to make a product real?
episodes.picture_concept: An illustrative phone circuit separates IC specification, fabrication, package, testing and delivery.
episodes.evidence_gate: Identify any claimed Qualcomm device/fab relationship with public BOM and company sources.

episodes.candidate_title: When Chip Designs Could Travel
episodes.narrative_tension: How did common design rules create an interface between people who draw chips and people who print them?
episodes.picture_concept: Several independently authored layouts converge onto an illustrative shared-wafer run and split into different designs.
episodes.evidence_gate: Attribute Mead–Conway, multi-project wafer practice and dates specifically; no claim that one textbook invented all design.

episodes.candidate_title: What Apple Designs—and What It Buys
episodes.narrative_tension: What can a system company control with its own silicon without owning a fabrication plant?
episodes.picture_concept: One product system opens into design choices, outsourced wafer processing and assembly; two types of control are outlined.
episodes.evidence_gate: Device and partner attribution require exact dates/generations; integrated manufacturing remains a real alternative.

episodes.candidate_title: The GPU Had Another Job
episodes.narrative_tension: A chip sold to draw game scenes becomes useful for a different class of parallel computation—what made that possible?
episodes.picture_concept: The same conceptual execution lanes shift from shading pixels to processing arrays, with architecture changes flagged.
episodes.evidence_gate: Do not claim gaming alone caused AI or that exact hardware/workloads are unchanged; verify product/software chronology.

episodes.candidate_title: A Working Transistor Wasn't Enough
episodes.narrative_tension: Can an impressive laboratory device become a reliable industrial component?
episodes.picture_concept: Point-contact amplification succeeds once, then an illustrative repeatability/ruggedness comparison changes the question.
episodes.evidence_gate: Device-specific historical records; do not pass reconstructed 'failed tests' off as observed experiments.

episodes.candidate_title: The Instruction That Left a Trace
episodes.narrative_tension: If a CPU discards speculative work, why can traces of that work remain observable?
episodes.picture_concept: Two parallel timelines separate architectural results from cache effects; a rejected path leaves a timed trace.
episodes.evidence_gate: Identify affected architectures, demonstrations and mitigations correctly; not 'every secret leaked'.

episodes.candidate_title: When Speed Wasn't the Only Measure
episodes.narrative_tension: How could lower switching power change which chip technology became valuable?
episodes.picture_concept: Complementary switching and rest current are compared under stated conditions; power flows instead of magic zero-power claims.
episodes.evidence_gate: Check early CMOS time, speed, leakage and dynamic power; avoid a single 'rejected' decision myth.

episodes.candidate_title: Free Instructions, Expensive Chips
episodes.narrative_tension: What is genuinely open in an ISA—and what still costs years of engineering?
episodes.picture_concept: One instruction splits into different cores; verification and physical implementation budgets remain separate.
episodes.evidence_gate: Distinguish ISA licensing, core IP, toolchain, verification and foundry expenditures.

episodes.candidate_title: Two GPUs, One Research Breakthrough
episodes.narrative_tension: Why did a particular multi-GPU and software setup matter in an ImageNet benchmark?
episodes.picture_concept: A dated experiment's training batches split between two boards; speed/memory assumptions and score labels appear only from original paper.
episodes.evidence_gate: Use original 2012 AlexNet paper and ImageNet evaluation; not 'beat every AI lab'.

episodes.candidate_title: When a Forecast Became a Deadline
episodes.narrative_tension: How can an expectation about future density synchronize firms that compete?
episodes.picture_concept: One date-stamped forecast becomes independently dated equipment/process/roadmap commitments; a late tool reveals tradeoffs.
episodes.evidence_gate: Separate Moore's 1965 claim from later industry roadmaps; coordination is interpretation, not a universal causal proof.

episodes.candidate_title: The Heat at the End of Faster
episodes.narrative_tension: When more switching ceases to be an affordable route, where does performance go?
episodes.picture_concept: Temperature and power envelopes constrain a CPU path; work migrates to parallelism, memory and software.
episodes.evidence_gate: Use qualitative simulations unless validated device/thermal numbers are sourced; do not imply all chips share one power wall.

episodes.candidate_title: Why Intel Left DRAM
episodes.narrative_tension: A manufacturer cannot spend the same capacity twice: which business gets the next wafer start?
episodes.picture_concept: One factory allocation board has two products and a constrained capacity slot; historical accounts are overlaid separately.
episodes.evidence_gate: Intel product and management histories; separate historical managerial recollection and contemporary financial records.

episodes.candidate_title: When a Bit Was Woven by Hand
episodes.narrative_tension: What did storing one bit demand from a human hand, a machine and a budget?
episodes.picture_concept: A thread passes through ferrite rings; a read pulse reveals the physical work of memory, without posing as archival footage.
episodes.evidence_gate: Confirm destructive read/restore for the illustrated core design, era and labor source.

episodes.candidate_title: Japan's Memory Bet Met a New Customer
episodes.narrative_tension: Why can superior qualification in one market fail to guarantee sales in a changing market?
episodes.picture_concept: Two dated customer requirement sheets flank a changing price/product-mix ledger; no single-cause verdict.
episodes.evidence_gate: Do not assert 'quality caused decline'; test PC-market demand, currency, trade and product strategy as competing factors.

episodes.candidate_title: The Gate That Defined Its Own Edges
episodes.narrative_tension: How does self-alignment change what a production process can repeat?
episodes.picture_concept: A single gate defines the subsequent boundary; overlay error in two schematic routes is contrasted without invented yield.
episodes.evidence_gate: Use actual silicon-gate process/patent history; distinguish geometry benefit from downstream commercialization.

episodes.candidate_title: Samsung's Cost of Learning DRAM
episodes.narrative_tension: Why would a late entrant keep spending before the next wafer becomes reliable?
episodes.picture_concept: An illustrative yield-improvement process is shown against a dated investment/learning timeline, with measured values only if sourced.
episodes.evidence_gate: Verify specific 'told it would fail' quotation; no fabricated Samsung yield numbers.

episodes.candidate_title: The Memory Chip With a Window
episodes.narrative_tension: Why would opening a package to light make software and hardware development easier?
episodes.picture_concept: UV reaches an illustrated EPROM die through quartz, then erase/program cycles make iteration visible.
episodes.evidence_gate: Distinguish UV EPROM from EEPROM/flash; avoid inventor dialogue without records.

episodes.candidate_title: The Bit That Keeps Forgetting
episodes.narrative_tension: How does a tiny capacitor hold a bit only by being continually cared for?
episodes.picture_concept: Charge leaks, a sense amplifier reads and restores, refresh repeats; die-area comparison is labeled illustrative.
episodes.evidence_gate: Verify classic 1T1C technical sources; no source-free cost-per-bit figures.

episodes.candidate_title: Inventing Flash Was Only the Beginning
episodes.narrative_tension: Why do a patent, a stable manufacturing process and a profitable market award value to different players?
episodes.picture_concept: An erase block is tested across reliability gates; product and customer pathways fork from invention.
episodes.evidence_gate: Separate early invention, NOR/NAND versions, manufacturing actors and market outcomes with dated sources.

episodes.candidate_title: The Rules Written Into an AI Chip
episodes.narrative_tension: How can a dated export-control threshold alter a product's configuration before shipment?
episodes.picture_concept: A historical rule sheet overlays an illustrative product-parameter card; classification changes across explicit dated versions.
episodes.evidence_gate: Find official 2022–23 provisions/revisions and scope; make no unverified claim about legality in Nov 2026.

episodes.candidate_title: The Crystal Behind Wartime Radar
episodes.narrative_tension: What did a defense buyer need from material purity and reliable detection?
episodes.picture_concept: A radar pulse weakens at a detector; one physical crystal/metal contact is studied as a labeled mechanism.
episodes.evidence_gate: War-period specific research and components; do not make radar the sole origin of the chip industry.

episodes.candidate_title: When a Material Exists but Isn't Qualified
episodes.narrative_tension: What is the time lag between getting a substitute chemical and running it safely in a process?
episodes.picture_concept: Material flows across a dated licensing line, then waits at a technical qualification gate before illustrative fab use.
episodes.evidence_gate: 2019 Japanese licensing is not a blanket global ban; dates, material types and adoption evidence required.

episodes.candidate_title: Copying the Chip Doesn't Copy the System
episodes.narrative_tension: What could replicating a specific device do—and what supporting capability remained difficult?
episodes.picture_concept: Two dated device photos/spec sheets meet a traced schematic; production capability is shown as a distinct chain.
episodes.evidence_gate: No invented single nationwide order; verify specific Soviet products, documentation and dependencies.

episodes.candidate_title: The Manufacturing Problem Rivals Shared
episodes.narrative_tension: What problem can competing chipmakers cooperate on without abandoning competition?
episodes.picture_concept: Separate fab samples arrive at one generic precompetitive test setup, then leave in different product lines.
episodes.evidence_gate: SEMATECH charter, membership and funding chronology; 'shared secrets' remains illustrative language.

episodes.candidate_title: Japan's Shared Research, Separate Companies
episodes.narrative_tension: Why does a shared R&D program not create one unified chipmaker?
episodes.picture_concept: An archival program map splits common research from proprietary manufacturing lines; compare precisely with SEMATECH.
episodes.evidence_gate: Use VLSI project records; do not claim all rivals shared one physical laboratory.

episodes.candidate_title: A Government That Bought Reliability
episodes.narrative_tension: How could the requirements of a demanding public customer reshape component adoption?
episodes.picture_concept: An illustrative purchased IC passes a documented test sequence before entering a system integration drawing.
episodes.evidence_gate: Distinguish NASA versus DoD procurement, device types and their separate historical roles.

episodes.candidate_title: How a Memory Price Became a Trade Case
episodes.narrative_tension: When did the price of a DRAM become evidence in an international dispute?
episodes.picture_concept: Dated price comparators enter an agreement and enforcement timeline; transaction, legal test and consequence split.
episodes.evidence_gate: Use original US–Japan agreement and trade case records; avoid treating contested price formulas as objective universal cost.
